wu: Students stand up. Teacher shows flashcards of free-time activities (playing football, reading books, cooking). Students walk around and ask each other: 'Do you like...?' and respond with 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'.
wuAlt: Teacher writes 'free time' on the board. Students brainstorm activities in pairs, writing 3 each on sticky notes and sticking them up.
Teacher mimes an activity (e.g., swimming). Students guess: 'Do you like swimming?' Teacher responds with 'Yes, I love it' or 'No, I enjoy reading'.
pres: Teacher presents 3 model sentences: 'I like playing football', 'I love reading books', 'I enjoy cooking'. Uses flashcards to show each activity. Checks understanding by asking: 'What do I love?' and 'Do I like cooking?'
presAlt: Teacher tells a short story: 'On weekends, I like walking in the park. I love drinking mint tea. I enjoy listening to music.' Underlines the -ing forms.
Teacher uses realia: a football, a book, a cooking pot. Holds each up and says the sentence, then gestures for students to repeat chorally.
prac: Students do 'Find Someone Who...' with a grid of activities. They walk around and ask: 'Do you like...?' and write names. Teacher monitors and models questions.
pracAlt: Students work in pairs. Teacher gives each pair a set of activity cards. They take turns saying: 'I like/love/enjoy...' and the partner responds with 'Me too' or 'I don't, I prefer...'.
Teacher plays 'Guess the Activity'. Mimes an activity; students guess using: 'Do you like...?' Teacher responds with 'Yes, I love it' or 'No, I enjoy...'
ls: Students listen to 3 short audio clips of people talking about their free time. They tick the activities mentioned on their worksheet. Teacher plays each clip twice.
re: Students stand in a circle. Teacher says an activity (e.g., 'swimming'), and students jump if they like it, squat if they don't. Quick and energetic.
prod: Students work in pairs. They plan their ideal weekend using 'I like/love/enjoy...'. They then present their plan to the class: 'On Saturday, I like... On Sunday, I love...'
rw: Students read 3 short profiles of people's free-time activities. They underline all the -ing forms. Then they write 4 sentences about their own free time using 'like/love/enjoy + -ing'.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a character's weekend using target language. Ends with the goodbye routine: 'Today we talked about free time. Thank you, class!'
g: Students match flashcards to sentences like 'I love swimming'.
Teacher labels corners of the room: 'love', 'like', 'enjoy'. Students go to the corner for an activity when called out.
Student mimes an activity; others guess using 'Do you like...?'
Students have bingo cards with activities. They ask classmates: 'Do you like...?' to mark off squares.
Student 1 says: 'I like playing football'. Student 2 repeats and adds: 'I love reading books'.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 6 sentences about their friends' free time.
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'I like ___. I love ___. I enjoy ___.'
hw: Write 5 sentences about your free time using like/love/enjoy + -ing.
Interview a family member about their free time and write 3 sentences.
Draw a picture of your ideal weekend and label 3 activities with -ing words.
tip: Connect activities to local context: ask about free time during Ramadan or holidays like Green March. Use real-life examples like 'liking mint tea with friends' to build rapport.
